_comment: Hand-curated cause_category lookup table. Maps each PlantVillage/PlantDoc disease class to its cause category (pathogen/pest/deficiency), pathogen/pest name, common symptoms, and recommended remedies. This is a MANUAL CURATION task -- the datasets do not provide this mapping automatically.

symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown lesions on leaves
remedies: Apply fungicide (captan, mancozeb) at green tip stage
Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves
Apple___Apple_scab.severity_notes: Mild if < 10% leaf area; severe if > 30% with fruit involvement

symptoms: Frogeye leaf spots (tan center, dark border)
Black, rotting fruit with concentric rings
remedies: Prune out dead and cankered wood
Maintain tree vigor with proper fertilization
Apple___Black_rot.severity_notes: Can destroy entire crop if left untreated in warm, humid conditions

symptoms: Bright orange/yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Spots on fruit in severe cases
remedies: Scout for galls on cedar trees in spring
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.severity_notes: Rarely kills trees but reduces fruit quality significantly

symptoms: Rectangular gray to tan lesions between leaf veins
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.severity_notes: Yield losses up to 40% in susceptible hybrids under high pressure

symptoms: Small, round to elongated brown/red pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules break open releasing powdery spores
remedies: Apply fungicide if pustules appear before tasseling
Scout fields regularly from V8 onwards
Most commercial hybrids have adequate resistance
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.severity_notes: Usually minor in resistant varieties; significant in sweet corn

symptoms: Long, elliptical gray-green to tan lesions (1-6 inches)
Can coalesce and kill entire leaves
remedies: Apply foliar fungicide at early infection
Plant resistant hybrids with Ht genes
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.severity_notes: Up to 30% yield loss if infection occurs before or during silking

symptoms: Tan spots with dark borders on leaves
Brown-black fruit rot; berries shrivel to hard mummies
remedies: Remove mummified berries and infected canes
Apply fungicide (mancozeb, myclobutanil) from bud break
Ensure good canopy management for air circulation
Sanitation is critical — remove all diseased tissue
Grape___Black_rot.severity_notes: Can destroy 80%+ of crop; most damaging grape disease in humid regions

symptoms: Sudden vine collapse (apoplexy) in severe cases
remedies: Protect pruning wounds with fungicide paste
Avoid large pruning wounds; use double-pruning technique
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).severity_notes: Chronic trunk disease; vines may survive years with declining yield

symptoms: Dark brown to reddish-brown spots on leaves
remedies: Ensure adequate spacing for air circulation
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.severity_notes: Usually moderate; mainly affects leaf quality, not directly fruit

symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target pattern) on older leaves
Premature defoliation starting from lower leaves
remedies: Rotate crops (3-year minimum away from solanaceous crops)
Ensure adequate soil fertility (stressed plants are more susceptible)
Potato___Early_blight.severity_notes: Yield reduction 20-30% typical; worse under hot, dry conditions with heavy dew

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves, rapidly expanding
White fuzzy sporulation on leaf undersides in humid conditions
remedies: Destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles
Monitor weather forecasts (>10 hours leaf wetness + cool temps = high risk)
Potato___Late_blight.severity_notes: CRITICAL — can destroy entire crop in days under favorable conditions (the Irish Potato Famine pathogen)

symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown/black
Severe defoliation exposing fruit to sunscald
remedies: Rotate crops (2+ years away from solanaceous crops)
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.severity_notes: Fruit quality severely affected; yield losses 10-50%

symptoms: Target-shaped spots (concentric rings) on older/lower leaves
remedies: Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash
Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil) starting at first fruit set
Tomato___Early_blight.severity_notes: Common and manageable; yield impact 20-40% if uncontrolled

symptoms: Large, water-soaked, dark lesions on leaves
remedies: Destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost)
Tomato___Late_blight.severity_notes: CRITICAL — same pathogen as potato late blight; can destroy crop in days

symptoms: Yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety mold on leaf undersides
remedies: Plant resistant varieties (many modern varieties carry Cf genes)
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.severity_notes: Mainly a greenhouse problem; field impact usually moderate

symptoms: Many small circular spots with dark borders and gray centers
Tiny black dots (pycnidia) visible in spot centers
remedies: Remove and destroy lower infected leaves
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.severity_notes: Very common; significant defoliation reduces fruit size and yield

symptoms: Leaves turn yellow and dry out
remedies: Apply miticide (abamectin) if population exceeds threshold
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural predators
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.severity_notes: Can cause rapid plant decline in hot, dry conditions; economic threshold ~5 mites/leaf

symptoms: Circular brown spots with concentric rings on leaves
Spots may coalesce into large necrotic areas
Can also affect stems and fruit
remedies: Rotate crops away from solanaceous hosts
Tomato___Target_Spot.severity_notes: Moderate to severe; worse in warm, humid conditions

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.pathogen_name: TYLCV (begomovirus, transmitted by whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
remedies: Control whitefly vector (neonicotinoid insecticides, reflective mulch, sticky traps)
Use insect-proof mesh/netting in seedling nurseries
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.severity_notes: SEVERE — no cure once infected; prevention through vector control is essential

symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green on leaves
remedies: Disinfect tools and hands (virus is extremely stable)
Do not smoke near plants (tobacco can carry ToMV)
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.severity_notes: Persistent; virus survives in soil and on surfaces for months/years

remedies: Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.severity_notes: Can cause significant quality and yield loss in bell peppers

symptoms: Irregular purple to brown spots on leaves
Spots may merge causing large necrotic areas
remedies: Remove old infected leaves in spring
Ensure good air circulation between plants
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.severity_notes: Reduces plant vigor and next year's yield; usually not fatal

symptoms: Sunken lesions on fruit with cracking
remedies: Apply copper sprays at leaf fall and early spring
Peach___Bacterial_spot.severity_notes: Significant fruit quality issue; worse in warm, humid climates

symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves and shoots
remedies: Apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate at first sign
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.severity_notes: Primarily cosmetic on leaves; fruit quality affected if severe

_metadata.created_by: Manual curation from plant pathology references
_metadata.note: This is a design decision, not automated data — document it in your report. The cause_category field (pathogen/pest/deficiency/none) is central to the diagnosis pipeline's output structure.
